## Six Flags Entertainment Corporation Reports 2026 Third Quarter Results


November 05, 2026


Download (opens in new window)


- *Net revenues of $1.17 billion, down 11.0% on a reported basis and up 1.4% on a same-park basis(3)*
- *Net loss attributable to Six Flags of $366.1 million, or $3.59 per diluted share, which included $687.7 million of non-cash impairment charges, compared with a loss of $1.19 billion in the prior-year quarter, which included a $1.52 billion non-cash impairment charge*
- *Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $493.2 million, down 11.1% on a reported basis and up 1.1% on a same-park basis(3)*
- *Net cash from operating activities year-to-date up 36.5% to $498.5 million*
- *Liquidity of $1.06 billion at quarter-end*


ARLINGTON, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Six Flags Entertainment Corporation (NYSE: FUN) (the “Company” or “Six Flags”), the largest regional amusement park operator in North America, today announced results for its 2026 third quarter ended September 27, 2026. Prior-year results include eight parks that Six Flags no longer operates in 2026: seven parks sold to EPR Properties prior to the start of 2026 park operations and one park in Bowie, Maryland that closed after the 2025 season. Same-park(3) results exclude those sold and closed parks in order to reflect the performance of the current operating portfolio and are presented as supplemental information alongside reported results.

**Message from the CEO**


“Safety remains our highest priority. Following the incident at Six Flags Over Georgia last month, we are cooperating fully with the ongoing investigation. We have launched a comprehensive review of ride safety across our entire portfolio, supported by independent third-party engineering and inspection specialists. Our robust safety programs and practices are designed to meet or exceed established industry standards. We will conduct this work thoroughly, looking for opportunities to further strengthen our approach to ride safety,” said John Reilly, President and Chief Executive Officer.


Mr. Reilly continued, “Our third quarter results reflect the progress we are making against our strategic priorities and the underlying strength of our portfolio. Through the first nine months of the year, we delivered double-digit growth in Adjusted EBITDA on a same-park basis, reflecting the cumulative impact of our efforts to improve execution, strengthen operations and manage costs effectively. We are particularly encouraged by the momentum in our regional pass offerings, which are helping unlock the unique advantages of our multi-park network. Guests are increasingly visiting parks beyond their home market, providing early evidence that our strategy is driving incremental visitation, deeper guest engagement and stronger loyalty across the portfolio. We remain confident in our strategy and the significant opportunity ahead to drive profitable growth and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders."


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights**


- Reported net revenues decreased $144.7 million, or 11.0%, because the prior-year quarter included the eight parks no longer operated. Same-park net revenues increased $16.5 million, or 1.4%, to $1.17 billion. The same-park increase reflected higher per capita spending (2), a $2.4 million increase in out-of-park revenues (2), primarily resorts, and 54 additional operating days, most of which reflected the later timing of Labor Day. These benefits were partly offset by the impact of a 0.2% decrease in attendance on a same-park basis.


- Attendance was 18.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, down 0.2% on a same-park basis compared to the third quarter of 2025. Higher season pass and membership visitation was offset by lower single-day visitation and fewer complimentary tickets. July 4 fell on a Saturday rather than a Friday, and wildfire-related air quality disruptions affected certain parks. Same-park third quarter operating days were 2,122, compared with 2,068.


- Operating costs and expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $676.8 million, compared with $772.4 million on a reported basis and $676.3 million on a same-park basis in the prior-year quarter. Same-park costs were essentially unchanged (up 0.1%) despite 54 additional operating days. Operating expenses decreased $51.1 million for the quarter on a reported basis, and selling, general and administrative expenses decreased $29.4 million on a reported basis compared to the prior year third quarter. Same-park operating expenses increased $29.4 million on higher full-time wages and benefits, higher operating supplies tied to added operating days and investment in the guest experience, and higher insurance costs related to claims incurred. Same-park selling, general and administrative expenses decreased $27.3 million, primarily on lower full-time wages, including lower equity compensation and severance, and lower technology costs.


- Net loss attributable to Six Flags was $366.1 million, or $3.59 per diluted share, compared with $1.19 billion on a reported basis, or $11.77 per diluted share, in the prior-year quarter, which included a $1.52 billion non-cash impairment charge. The non-cash impairment charges in the current-year quarter totaled $687.7 million.


- Adjusted EBITDA (1) for the third quarter of 2026 was $493.2 million, a decrease of $61.5 million, or 11.1%, on a reported basis and an increase of $5.4 million, or 1.1%, on a same-park basis.


- Same-park per capita spending (2) for the third quarter increased 1.3% to $60.51. Same-park admissions per capita spending (2) rose $0.54, or 1.7%, to $32.07, and same-park in-park product per capita spending (2) rose $0.21, or 0.7%, to $28.44. Realized pricing and fewer complimentary tickets were contributing factors to the same-park increase.


**Nine Month 2026 Highlights**


- Reported net revenues decreased $186.6 million, or 7.6%, because the prior-year first nine months included the eight parks no longer operated. Same-park net revenues for the first nine months increased $61.6 million, or 2.8%, to $2.26 billion. The same-park increase reflected a 1.5% increase in attendance, higher per capita spending (2), and a $6.0 million increase in out-of-park revenues (2), primarily from one-time revenue events related to international agreements and out-of-park events. There was a 14 operating day decrease on a same-park basis.


- Attendance was 34.2 million for the first nine months of 2026, up 1.5% on a same-park basis compared to the first nine months of 2025. The increase was attributable to higher season pass and membership visitation as a result of a larger active pass base and higher cross park visitation.


- Operating costs and expenses for the first nine months of 2026 decreased $212.0 million, or 11.2%, on a reported basis compared to the first nine months of 2025. On a same-park basis for the first nine months, operating costs and expenses decreased $35.8 million, or 2.1%. Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased $46.0 million for the nine months on a reported basis, and operating expenses decreased $145.1 million on a reported basis compared to the prior nine month period. Same-park selling, general and administrative expenses decreased $41.1 million, primarily on lower full-time wages, including equity compensation, and lower advertising costs. The lower same-park basis selling, general and administrative expenses were somewhat offset by a $4.7 million increase in same-park operating expenses on higher insurance costs, higher costs for operating supplies tied to investment in the guest experience, and increased costs of utilities somewhat offset by less severance costs.


- Net loss attributable to Six Flags was $837.3 million on a reported basis, or $8.23 per diluted share, compared with $1.51 billion, or $14.99 per diluted share, for the first nine months of the prior year, which included a $1.52 billion non-cash impairment charge. The current year included non-cash impairment charges totaling $726.3 million.


- Adjusted EBITDA (1) for the first nine months decreased $13.3 million, or 2.1%, on a reported basis and increased $61.8 million, or 10.7%, on a same-park basis.


- Same-park per capita spending (2) for the first nine months increased 1.0% to $62.13. Same-park admissions per capita spending (2) rose $0.07, or 0.2%, to $33.21, and same-park in-park product per capita spending (2) rose $0.52, or 1.8%, to $28.92.


**Season Pass and Membership**


- Season passes and memberships are tracked together as the active pass base: the number of passholders and members who can visit the parks at a given time.


- At September 27, 2026, the active pass base was 7.1 million, up about 469,000 units, or 7.1%, on a same-park basis versus last year. Passholders and members made up about 61% of same-park attendance in the third quarter of 2026.


- Year-to-date pass and membership sales on a same-park basis rose 134,000 units, or 2.8%, with average price up 2.0%.


- The 2027 pass program launched in early August, two weeks later than last year. 2027 passes are also valid for the rest of the 2026 season, so an early launch lets guests use one pass for most of two seasons, and some skip buying in alternate years. Launching later reduces that overlap and encourages guests to buy every year. As a result, 2027 sales to date reflect two fewer weeks of selling than last year's program at the same point.


- Passes expire each season, so the base is seasonally lower at the start of the year. Six Flags forecasts to enter 2027 with approximately 3.7 million active passholders and members on a same-park basis, flat to slightly up low single digits versus last year.


**Balance Sheet, Liquidity and Capital Allocation**


- Net cash from operating activities for the first nine months of 2026 was $498.5 million, an increase of $133.3 million from the prior-year period. Capital expenditures were $241.2 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with $408.1 million for the prior-year period.


- Cash and cash equivalents were $267.9 million at September 27, 2026. Total liquidity at the end of the third quarter was $1.06 billion, including $792.8 million available under the revolving credit facility, with no revolver borrowings outstanding.


- Total debt was $4.91 billion at September 27, 2026, a decrease of $275.0 million from December 31, 2025. Net debt (4) was $4.66 billion at September 27, 2026.


- Total deferred revenue was $331.3 million at September 27, 2026, a decrease of $34.0 million from September 28, 2025, largely due to the parks no longer operated. At the parks operated in both periods, deferred revenue decreased $14.4 million, or 4.2%, largely due to an increased mix of memberships beyond the initial 12-month commitment period resulting in greater recurring monthly revenue and due to the later launch of 2027 season pass sales, as well as lower sponsorship deferred revenue due to a one-time benefit in the prior year.


- Six Flags now expects 2026 capital expenditures of $350.0 million to $375.0 million, compared with its prior expectation of $400.0 million to $425.0 million. The reduction comes from the timing of large new ride projects, not from maintenance.


**Outlook**


- October was softer than planned driven by unfavorable weather on several of the biggest weekends early in the month and by the impact of the tragic incident at Six Flags Over Georgia and related proactive ride closures.


- Six Flags currently expects about 60 additional operating days in the fourth quarter versus last year, driven mainly by the return of Holiday in the Park winter events.


- With October results in hand, Six Flags now expects fourth quarter 2026 same-park Adjusted EBITDA (1) to be between $140 and $150 million compared with fourth quarter 2025 same-park Adjusted EBITDA of $167 million.


**Conference Call**


Six Flags will host a conference call and audio webcast to discuss third quarter 2026 financial results at 8 a.m. ET today, November 5, 2026. A live audio webcast of the call, a supplemental presentation and, shortly after the call, a replay will be available on the Six Flags Investors website at[https://investors.sixflags.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Finvestors.sixflags.com&esheet=54635727&newsitemid=20261105329965&lan=en-US&anchor=https%3A%2F%2Finvestors.sixflags.com&index=1&md5=a12a396b34429fd0b5770fe80798fcbb) under Investor Information / Events & Presentations.


**About Six Flags Entertainment Corporation**


Six Flags Entertainment Corporation (NYSE: FUN) is the largest regional amusement park operator in North America, with 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resort properties across 13 U.S. states, Canada, and Mexico. The Company also manages an amusement park in Saudi Arabia. Focused on its purpose of creating FUN, thrills and a lifetime of memories, Six Flags provides immersive entertainment to millions of guests every year with world-class coasters, themed rides, thrilling water parks, resorts and a portfolio of beloved intellectual property such as Looney Tunes®, DC Comics® and PEANUTS®.


**Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


This release includes measures that are not calculated in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”): Modified EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA; per capita spending, admissions per capita spending, in-park product per capita spending, in-park revenues and out-of-park revenues; Same-Park Basis measures; and net debt. Each is presented with, and reconciled in the tables that follow to, the most directly comparable GAAP measure for each period presented. These measures should not be considered in isolation or as substitutes for GAAP measures, and they may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies.


(1)


**Adjusted EBITDA and Modified EBITDA.** Modified EBITDA represents earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, other non-cash items and other adjustments as defined in the Company’s credit agreement. Adjusted EBITDA represents Modified EBITDA less net income (loss) attributable to non-controlling interests. The most directly comparable GAAP measure is net income (loss). Management believes these measures are meaningful measures of park-level operating profitability and uses them to measure returns on capital investments, evaluate potential acquisitions, determine awards under incentive compensation plans and calculate compliance with certain loan covenants. Adjusted EBITDA is also widely used by analysts and investors to evaluate operating performance on a consistent basis.


(2)


**Per capita measures.** Per capita spending is calculated as revenues generated within the Company’s amusement parks and separately gated outdoor water parks, along with related parking revenues and online transaction fees charged to customers (in-park revenues), divided by total attendance. Admissions per capita spending is calculated as in-park admissions revenues divided by total attendance. In-park product per capita spending is calculated as all other in-park revenues, including food and beverage, merchandise, games and extra-charge offerings, divided by total attendance. Out-of-park revenues are revenues from resorts, out-of-park food and merchandise locations, sponsorships, international agreements and all other out-of-park operations. The most directly comparable GAAP measure is net revenues. Management uses these measures as major factors in significant operational decisions because they are primary drivers of financial and operational performance, measuring demand, pricing and consumer behavior.


(3)


**Same-Park Basis.** Same-Park Basis compares the performance of the Company’s current operating portfolio and excludes the results of (a) the seven parks sold to EPR Properties prior to the start of 2026 park operations and (b) the combined amusement and water park in Bowie, Maryland, where operations were discontinued after the 2025 season (together, the “parks sold and closed”). Same-Park Basis measures, including net revenues, net income (loss), diluted income (loss) per share, Adjusted EBITDA, operating costs and expenses, attendance and per capita measures, are presented alongside the corresponding reported GAAP measures, and the amounts attributable to the parks sold and closed are shown in the tables that follow. Management believes Same-Park Basis information is meaningful to evaluate operating performance of the parks owned and operated in both periods and uses it for that purpose.


(4)


**Net debt.** Net debt is long-term debt, including current maturities, plus unamortized debt issuance costs and original issue discount, less acquisition fair value layers, less cash and cash equivalents. The most directly comparable GAAP measure is long-term debt, including current maturities. Management and investors use net debt to monitor leverage.


The Company has not provided a reconciliation of forward-looking Adjusted EBITDA to net income (loss), the most directly comparable GAAP measure, because it cannot do so without unreasonable efforts. Net income (loss) depends on items that are inherently uncertain or outside the Company’s control, including non-cash impairment charges, foreign currency gains or losses, and gains or losses on asset sales, the probable significance of which is that net income (loss) could differ materially from Adjusted EBITDA.

(c)


Consists of certain costs as defined in the Company's credit agreement. These costs are added back to net loss to calculate Modified EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA and include certain legal and consulting expenses; certain costs at the sold and closed parks; certain recruiting and relocation costs; cost of goods sold recorded to align inventory standards following the merger; administrative payments related to the Partnership Parks; Mexican VAT taxes on intercompany activity; and contract termination costs. This balance also includes unrealized gains and losses on pension assets and short-term investments.
